headline: Airbnb Recreates K3G's Raichand House in Mumbai, Bookings Open November 23
subheadline: For the film's 25th anniversary, Airbnb's free two-hour 'At Home with the Raichands' experience runs December 1–6 in Mumbai with 180 invitations — the grand staircase, the family study and Poo's closet, rebuilt for fans.
body:
• Airbnb has recreated the Raichand House from Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (K3G) in Mumbai as "At Home with the Raichands," a two-hour experience marking the Hindi film's 25th anniversary.
  • Booking requests open on Monday, November 23, 2026 at 12 p.m. IST at airbnb.com/k3g — the experience is priced at ₹0 and runs December 1–6, 2026.
  • Only 180 invitations are available; each spot covers one guest plus a companion, and guests must arrange their own travel to Mumbai.
  • To request a spot you need an active Airbnb profile with a history of positive reviews and a government-issued ID — and the hosts, Karan Johar, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Hrithik Roshan, will not appear in person.

Twenty-five years after Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham introduced the Raichand family to audiences, Airbnb is opening the doors of their house. The company has recreated the fictional Raichand House in Mumbai as At Home with the Raichands, a two-hour immersive experience built around the film's grand staircase, family study and Poo's closet, Airbnb announced. The experience, part of the company's Only on Airbnb series and made with Dharma Productions, runs from December 1 to 6, 2026, with 180 invitations in total.

Plan Your Visit

  • Dates: December 1–6, 2026, Mumbai
  • Experience: At Home with the Raichands — a two-hour visit to the recreated Raichand House
  • Booking requests open: Monday, November 23, 2026 at 12 p.m. IST at airbnb.com/k3g
  • Admission: ₹0 — priced at zero by Airbnb; guests pay their own travel to and from Mumbai
  • Spots: 180 invitations; each spot covers one guest plus one companion
  • Requirements: Active Airbnb profile with a history of positive reviews, and a government-issued ID
  • Note: Karan Johar, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Hrithik Roshan host the experience in name — Airbnb states the experience does not include their appearance

What guests will see

Airbnb says the visit begins with an entry test drawn from the film — a tongue twister guests must attempt before stepping in — followed by a traditional Raichand-style welcome and the grand staircase entrance. An immersive audio tour leads through the living room and the family study, and a separate space recreates Poo's closet, the wardrobe of Kareena Kapoor Khan's character. Guests can write a note to someone special, in the spirit of the film's family theme, and leave with a keepsake. The recreated rooms cover the film's most quoted settings: the staircase, the study and the closet, Storyboard18 reported.

"To see the Raichand House come alive with Airbnb, and to give people the chance to actually walk through a world we've all spent so many years imagining, is incredibly special."

— Karan Johar, director, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham

The film, and why a house became an experience

Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham, released in 2001, is a Hindi-language family drama directed by Karan Johar, with Kareena Kapoor Khan as Poo and Hrithik Roshan as Rohan Raichand. Airbnb is marking 25 years of the film, and its India head framed the house itself as the draw. "For 25 years, Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham has brought generations together through its characters, music and its timeless message about family and belonging," said Amanpreet Singh Bajaj, Country Head, Airbnb India and Southeast Asia. "The Raichand House is one of those fictional homes that audiences have grown up with and come to feel connected to." Kapoor Khan said Poo "had her own sense of style, her own vocabulary and, most importantly, she never really needed anyone's approval," and that fans can now "step into her world, explore her closet." Roshan said seeing the house recreated, and fans walking through it, was "the best way to celebrate the film."

How to request a spot

Requests open at noon IST on Monday, November 23 at airbnb.com/k3g, and Airbnb stresses the process is not a competition. You need an active Airbnb profile with a history of positive reviews, and every guest requesting a spot must be able to provide a government-issued ID. The experience itself costs nothing, but travel to Mumbai is on you — for diaspora fans, that means treating this as a reason to time a December trip home, with the request window opening nine days before the first session. With 180 spots across six days, expect the window to close fast.
